finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a caller-supplied URL. Its only check is a suffix test, `host.endswith("example.com")`. The check has no leading dot, and the defined ALLOWED_SUFFIX constant (".example.com") is never used. Any attacker-registered domain ending in `example.com` passes, for example `evilexample.com`. The attacker can point that domain's DNS at 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or an RFC-1918 address, so the server makes the request to an internal target. The check is a suffix match, not strict set membership, so it does not close the finding. The response body is not returned, only `len(r.text)`, so this is semi-blind. Status code and length still leak, and timing allows port and host probing. Severity is MEDIUM. Redirect risk is no: httpx.AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default and the code does not set follow_redirects. The DNS-rebinding concern remains for any allowlisted host.

finding.guards_checked: Suffix check on parsed .hostname at mirror.py:13. It is not strict set membership, lacks the dot boundary, and does not restrict scheme or resolved IP. No authentication on the route. No IP or CIDR egress blocking in the repo. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass is not present. /ping (mirror.py:20-24) uses a hardcoded URL and was not flagged.

verdict.guard_found: Only `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, a suffix check with no dot boundary. It does not close the finding. There is no auth, scheme restriction or IP blocking.
verdict.reason: The query param `url` (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and unauthenticated, the only guard is the non-closing suffix check at mirror.py:13 (so `evilexample.com` passes), and the original URL reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 with only `len(r.text)` returned at mirror.py:17.
